roots = [r for r in explicit if r not in orphaned]

# A harness that does neither leaves us to find ourselves. An installed plugin
# lives under the harness's own directory in the user's home, in one of a few
# shapes. This registration's own harness comes first, then any other; within
# one directory the highest version wins, compared by number ("1.10.0" beats
# "1.9.0"), and a copy the harness marked orphaned is skipped. Harness

        ("plugins", "cache", "*", plugin),
        ("plugins", "marketplaces", market),
        ("plugins", plugin),
    ):
        found = glob.glob(os.path.join(home, harness, *shape))
        found = [p for p in found if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(p, ".orphaned_at"))]

forge_ledger.py asks the forge for the login at exactly 3 sites: reconstruct_state (830-834), _trusted_set (1793-1800) and RationaleReader._identity (2169-2182); each takes `user`, else `username`, else `login`, through _author (790-793).

The trusted set is the --trust values plus the live login when it is non-empty; the rejected set is the --reject values; an author in both raises UsageError (exit 3). --trust/--reject are repeatable flags on reconstruct, post, reply, resolve, summary, gate, rationale-post, rationale-verify and rationale-read; trailers, rationale-add and rationale-drop take none.

reconstruct_state is reached from every settle command: reconstruct (2427), post (1297, 1371), reply (1036, 1098), resolve (1112), summary (1401), gate (1492) and _repair_all_pending (1230); _trusted_set from rationale-post (1917) and rationale-verify (2003); RationaleReader only from rationale-read (2378).

The settle ledger refuses unclassified authors: an unedited marker-bearing note whose author is in neither set raises LedgerError `unclassified_authors` (exit 2); a rejected author's marker note is counted ignored_untrusted; an edited marker note raises edited_markers.

Rationale scope differs from the settle ledger: rationale-post and rationale-verify count only trusted, unedited notes and list other authors in excluded.untrusted without refusing; rationale-read uses label mode, counting every author but rejected ones and labelling each self, trusted or other.

identity.json lives at <base>/<sha1(git common dir, AFK_CFG_FORGE, origin URL)[:16]>/identity.json, base = AFK_RATIONALE_CACHE, else $XDG_CACHE_HOME/afk/rationale, else ~/.cache/afk/rationale; a base inside the repository raises. Only rationale-read writes it, after a live auth-status returns a non-empty user and --no-cache is absent; it uses the cached user only when --offline is set or the live call raised.
identity.json has no age limit on read; json files older than 7 days are deleted only at the first cache write of a process, so an --offline run, which writes nothing, can use an identity of any age.
reconstruct_state and _trusted_set never read identity.json; they call auth-status live on every run.

Adapter.call raises LedgerError when bash is missing, on timeout (AFK_LEDGER_ADAPTER_TIMEOUT, default 120 s, a non-number falls back), on a non-zero exit, on stdout that is not one JSON object, and on an answer carrying error/unsupported/unavailable. Settle commands then exit 2; rationale-post/verify return blocked forge-unavailable; rationale-read records `offline:` and falls back to the cached identity.
Inference from the two facts above: with an empty login, reconstruct refuses any change that already carries a marker note by the developer unless the caller passes that login in --trust.

Adapter.call runs bash -c '. $AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/lib/adapter.sh; afk_adapter forge "$1"' with the payload on stdin; AFK_LEDGER_ADAPTER_CMD replaces that with shlex.split(value) + [verb]. afk_adapter takes the kind from AFK_CFG_FORGE, the directory adapters/forge/<kind>, the entry from adapter.json runner.entry, and runs `bash forge.sh <verb>`. This repository selects forge: github.
The trust comparison is a string match of the note `author` against the login: GitHub notes carry user.login and GitLab notes author.username, the same fields auth-status returns.

claims.text: auth-status runs `gh auth status` then `gh api user --jq .login` (github) or `glab auth status` then `glab api user` .username (gitlab), and prints {authenticated:true, user} with the captured stdout put unescaped into `user`; neither branch checks the exit status of the `api user` call. Each CLI call is limited to AFK_FORGE_TIMEOUT (default 60 s) where GNU timeout exists; a missing CLI answers unavailable and exits 4; forge: none answers unsupported and exits 3.

On GitHub a `gh api user --jq .login` that exits non-zero after a passing `gh auth status` is not caught by the adapter: gh writes the HTTP error body to stdout (probe: Bad credentials, 5-line JSON, exit 1), the adapter still answers authenticated:true with that body as `user` and exits 0, so the answer spans 5 lines and parse_adapter_output raises LedgerError `adapter wrote extra stdout`. An error body on one line that holds a double quote makes the answer invalid JSON and raises `adapter returned invalid JSON`.
